summary:
STILL LISTENING
3D Sci-Fi Action & Adventure Game | 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge

We developed STILL LISTENING, a 3D sci-fi action-adventure game inspired by NASA’s 2026 Space Apps Challenge: Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA’s Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.

Players battle alien creatures across extraterrestrial worlds to free abandoned NASA spacecraft and bring them back to life. Meticulously modeled after real NASA hardware, each liberated machine shares its history, original purpose, and scientific achievements—directly addressing the challenge by giving forgotten equipment a voice, identity, and emotional bond with players.

Immersive sound effects and dynamic voiceovers accompany every action. Players personalize their journey by naming and customizing both their avatar and spacecraft, while progressive difficulty levels welcome all ages and skill levels. Each stage features a distinct 3D celestial environment where gravity, climate, and terrain directly shape movement, mechanics, and mission challenges.

An integrated AI Agent powered by NASA’s database lets players explore verified space history, alongside in-game trivia unlocking bonus points and rewards. This matters because it turns passive history into hands-on learning—teaching real planetary physics, inspiring curiosity for space exploration, and ensuring these silent pioneers are never forgotten.

STILL LISTENING — Every machine has a story worth hearing.
details:
N1 Solution

STILL LISTENING is an interactive 3D browser game built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Its purpose is to make space history engaging and accessible by turning retired NASA hardware on the Moon and Mars—specifically Apollo 11 Eagle, Surveyor 3, Viking 1, Ingenuity, and Opportunity—into the central focus of a playable rescue mission rather than passive archival entries.

How does it Work:

Players start by setting up a profile (name, age, avatar, rover choice, and difficulty mode). They then drive across two distinct 3D environments—the Moon and Mars—to defend stranded NASA landers and rovers from enemy scavengers and reconnect them into a communication relay chain. Each environment alters gameplay mechanics: the Moon features low-gravity jumps and ground-based enemies, while Mars introduces dust storms, seismic shockwaves, and slope-tilt hazards. Rescuing each spacecraft unlocks a visual hologram card with verified NASA mission facts, synthesized audio/voice narration, a quick trivia check, and an interactive in-game Q&A archive (AURA) where players can explore each machine's history.

Benefits of the Game

  • Bite-Sized STEM Education: Presents real NASA landing coordinates, mission timelines, and discoveries through clean visual stat cards and trivia instead of dense text.
  • Story-Driven Engagement: Connects players emotionally to the real history of NASA's retired missions—culminating in Opportunity reactivating to restore the final signal.
  • Easy Access & Playability: Runs directly in a standard web browser with no installation required, offering three difficulty levels (Cadet, Ranger, Commander) and assisted laser targeting so players of different ages can play smoothly.

Our Goal

Our goal is to preserve the legacy of NASA’s abandoned lunar and Martian explorers through interactive storytelling—sparking curiosity about planetary science and inspiring players to learn more about the real missions that paved the way for future space exploration.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Coding Languages & Web Technologies:
    • HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+): Core game logic, UI overlays, state management, and interactive Q&A archive.
    • Three.js (WebGL): Real-time 3D terrain generation, lighting, particle dust effects, rover movement, and spacecraft models.
    • Web Audio API & Web Speech API: Browser-native synthesized sound effects (lasers, explosions, radio chimes) and voice narration.
    • NASA Science Mission Archives (science.nasa.gov): Verified mission timelines, landing coordinates, hardware specifications, and historical discoveries for Apollo 11, Surveyor 3, Viking 1, Ingenuity, and Opportunity.
    • Design: Used to brainstorm mission pacing, structure clear UI/UX layouts for the hologram data cards, and generate visual/audio clips for our 30-second demo video.
    • Implementation Guidance: Used to structure the Three.js scene setup, implement gravity and slope-tilt variables, and organize verified NASA facts into interactive in-game Q&A prompts.
    • Debugging Assistance: Used to resolve Three.js CDN loading fallbacks, refine laser-to-target collision detection, and fix browser audio/speech compatibility issues.
